does: Opens a round of pita and spreads a thin layer of raw, spiced meat mixture inside, then presses the bread shut, so that the filling cooks and the bread crisps and soaks up its juices on the heat.

intro.what: This arayes-style preparation spreads a thin meat filling inside pita before cooking.
intro.why: It teaches you to make a flat even filling rather than a thick mound beneath delicate bread.

how: Cut round the edge of the pita with a knife, or split it along one side, and open it into layers.
Spread the filling thinly and evenly over the inner face of one layer, right to the edge.
Close the pita over the filling and press it down firmly with the hand, so that the layers hold together.
Cut it in half, or leave it whole, and cook it at once.

cues.text: The filling lies flat and even, with none showing at the edge.
The closed bread is firm and flat under the hand, and does not slide apart.

mistakes.mistake: Piling the filling thick in the middle, so that the bread crisps and burns before the filling is done.
mistakes.fix: Spread it thin, as thin as a finger, and even.

mistakes.mistake: Using a dry, cracked pita that splits as it is opened.
mistakes.fix: Warm the bread first, so that it bends.

quiz.question: Why distribute the filling evenly inside pita?
choices: To avoid a thick centre beneath faster-browning bread.
To concentrate nearly all the meat in the middle.
To leave empty bread across most of the surface.
quiz.because: A thin even layer reduces the contrast between thick filling and the bread surrounding it.

quiz.question: What happens after spreading the filling?
choices: Leave the layers loose and sliding.
Close the bread and press it firmly flat.
Add a tall extra mound before closing.
quiz.because: Firm flat contact holds the layers together around the distributed filling.

quiz.question: Which feel suggests the filled pita is assembled neatly?
choices: A raised loose centre under a shifting top.
A cracked shell around an uneven lump.
Flat and firm without layers sliding apart.
quiz.because: A stable flat shape indicates that the filling and bread are in even contact.

quiz.question: The pita cracks as it is opened. What should change?
choices: Warm it first so it bends.
Pull the brittle layers apart more sharply.
quiz.because: A little warmth makes the bread more flexible for opening without splitting.

variant_of.differs: The pocket is a round of bread, and the filling is raw meat spread flat as a thin layer and pressed shut so that it cooks with the bread. It is not packed into a hollow of a bird or a vegetable.
